review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Opinions are divided whether school should reward the students who achieve the best academic performance or those who show their constant improvements. Personally, I reckon that school authorities should reward both of them.

Admittedly, it is obvious that the rewards are belonged to the students who have excellent academic gains. Initially, they are the one who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, accordingly, they deserve their praises and privileges. This, in fact, may encourages these students to try harder to win their rewards, propelling towards their overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspects of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. It means that students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve success and experiences in later stage of life.

However, I believe that students who perform improvement should be praised. This primarily because only a few smart students can come first and received the rewards, which causes others to think that their effort is futile since they can not surpass those outstanding individuals and may make them lose their incentive to study. Furthermore, this can even emphasizing improvements, not only encourage all students to be diligent in their studies but also help students to understand when they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. As a result, this boosts the constant desire to outdo themselves may even benefits themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both individuals who have the excellent achievements and those who try their best should be rewarded equally. As it would be unfair to deny the success of one in favour of the others.

paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward students with the best academic performance or whether it is more important to reward students who show progress. I believe that school authorities should reward both groups.

Admittedly, students with excellent academic results deserve rewards. Since they have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage them and other students to study harder, thereby contributing to overall academic gains. Moreover, competition exists in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Becoming familiar with this reality can help students thrive in the face of fierce competition, and this may prepare them better for success and help them gain experience in a later stage of life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. This is primarily because, if only a few high-achieving students can come first and receive rewards, other students may think that further effort is futile because they cannot surpass these outstanding individuals. As a result, they may lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, recognizing improvement can encourage all students to work diligently and to understand that they need to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. This boosts the desire to outdo themselves, which may even benefit students more than competing against others.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students who achieve excellent academic results and those who make progress. It would be unfair to deny the success of one group in favour of the other.

paragraphs: Some individuals nowadays believe that public museums and art galleries will no longer be needed as historical objects and artworks can be viewed on a computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, developed technologies provide useful access to cultural and historical resources. With high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, viewers can explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving their homes. One clear example is the Louvre museum, which offers an online walkthrough that audiences can view on a screen. This can spread knowledge of art and culture to a wider audience. As a result, viewers may develop a broader appreciation of historical objects and artworks. In this way, those who cannot afford to travel there or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries play a key role in society. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing artefacts or artworks in person. Seeing these objects directly can evoke a sense of authenticity and emotions that digital images cannot convey. This can be seen in Quang Ninh museum in Vietnam, where tattered and worn-out uniforms worn by Vietnamese soldiers during the Vietnam War are displayed. Seeing these uniforms may help visitors feel empathy for what the soldiers went through. Equally importantly, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. They can attract tourists and foster bonding within the community.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that traditional museums and art exhibitions are still essential in today’s world. Therefore, relying solely on the Internet cannot replace direct visits to these places.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some individuals nowadays prefer visiting public museums and art galleries than in person. In this essay, however I am to refute this school of thought.

Admittedly, developed technologies yield beneficial cultural and historical approach. With high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, museums and art exhibitions not only enable viewers to explore the masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable details without leaving their home. One clear example is the Louvre museums, which uses Artificial intelligent to offer audience the online walkthrough just by a screen, in order to spread valuable culture and experience. As a result, people may developed a boundless eye for the historical objects and works of art exhibited on screen. In this way, those who cannot cannot afford to travel there directly or having mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries plays a key role in the society. Online experience, initially cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefacts or artworks in person, which evoke a sense of authenticity and emotions that digital images cannot convey. This can be seen in Quang Ninh museum in Vietnam, a place where tattered and worn-out uniforms worn by Vietnamese soldiers during the Vietnam war are displayed, which might bring people empathy for what the soldiers had gone through. Equally importantly, museums and galleries play as a vital cultural hubs, symbolizing the cultural identity of a region, they are not only a magnet for tourism but also a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I firmly convinced that traditional museums and art exhibitions are still essential in today's world. Therefore, using solely Internet to explore them is not a wise decision

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some individuals believe that it is encouraged for children to learn through trial and errors, while others think that adults play a vital role in helping the children avoiding mistakes. Personally, I am of the former school of thought because children should have freedom to make mistake, provided that errors do not involve serious damages.

On the one hand, opponents of the trial-and-errors approach often empathize that the adults should prevent the mistake before they can happen. This is predicted, initially, on the assumption that most mistakes are minor and avoidable, such as knives, electricity and fire, which are unnecessary to get hurt from. Thus, children should be educated to be careful with their surrounding. Furthermore, it is parents’ responsibility to shed children from harms, not only forestall mistakes but also fulfill this duty. They might believe that this can pre-emptively help little ones and gives parents peace of their mind because they have done their best to protect and raise their kids.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasons. In their opinions, parents can not be around their children all the time, this means that they have the opportunities to experience with new things, which is inevitable to make mistake. Moreover, young generation can learn from mistakes, helping them stand a good stead in the future. If children are shed from everything, they would grow up over dependent on others, which are undesirable traits.

Overall, it seems to me that giving a youngsters chances to learn from mistakes can prepare them for their bright future. Therefore, this also provided that parents should intervene and give guidance only on important matters and preventing errors that may derail their future.

completion.comment: Đủ trang đã gán, có mở bài, hai thân bài và kết bài; nhận xét dựa trên chữ cuối cùng nhìn thấy.

review.overall: Em giữ được hai phía, lập trường có điều kiện và gần đủ bảy nhánh của dàn ý. Bài có nỗ lực triển khai, nhưng còn nhiều cụm ghép chưa đúng: “mistakes are minor and avoidable” rồi lấy dao/lửa làm ví dụ, “shed children from harms”, “not only forestall mistakes but also fulfill this duty”. Em cần sửa chủ thể và quan hệ nghĩa, không chỉ thay từ cho trôi hơn.

paragraphs: Some individuals believe children should be encouraged to learn through trial and error, while others think adults play a vital role in helping them avoid mistakes. Personally, I am of the former school of thought: children should have the freedom to make mistakes, provided that those errors do not involve serious harm.

On the one hand, opponents of the trial-and-error approach often emphasize that adults should prevent avoidable mistakes before they occur. This view is predicated on the assumption that many mistakes are avoidable: children need not be hurt by knives, electricity or fire to learn to be careful. Furthermore, parents have a responsibility to shield children from harm, and forestalling such mistakes helps them fulfil that duty. Pre-emptively helping children can also give parents peace of mind since they know they have done their best to protect and raise them.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasons. In their view, parents cannot be around their children all the time; therefore, children have opportunities to experience new things, and some mistakes are inevitable. Moreover, young people can learn from those mistakes, and the lessons may stand them in good stead in the future. If children are shielded from everything, they may become overdependent on others, which is an undesirable trait.

Overall, giving youngsters chances to learn from mistakes can prepare them for a bright future, provided that parents intervene and give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail that future.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 1
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.
The graph below shows the three different kinds of emission sources (oil/coal/gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK.
Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
Write at least 150 words.

images.alt: Biểu đồ khí thải từ oil, coal và gas tại Anh, 1990–2010

paragraphs: The given bar graph illustrates the carbon emissions source from three specific fossil fuels in a 20-year period, from 1990 to 2010 in the UK.
Overall, it is clear that in the beginning period, coal contributed the highest amount of carbon. Also of note is that, the gas fuel had the highest carbon at the end of the examined time.

To elaborate, in 1990 an impressive more than 300 million tons of coal were found in the UK, which gradually decreased over the years and hit the lowest point of the chart (nearly 190 millions) in 2010. By contrast, the amount of gas, on the other hand, starting at only approximate 200 millions in 1990, slowly increased to the highest amount in 2010 (300 millions). This number was equal to the amount of coal in 1990.

Regarding of the oil, which was nearly 275 million tons in 1990, experiencing a flunction from 1995 to 2000 (nearly 250 declined to 255). At the end of the timeline, this number gradually decreased to roughly 200 million tons.
review.overall: Cô thấy em đã tìm được sự đổi ngôi giữa coal và gas. Tuy nhiên overview cần nói trực tiếp gas tăng, coal giảm và oil giảm nhìn cả kỳ nhưng tăng lại một lần giữa kỳ. Khi tả số liệu, em cần đặt đúng đại lượng là khí thải; đặc biệt không thể viết “nearly 250 declined to 255” vì số sau cao hơn số trước. Em hãy sửa câu oil thành một câu đầy đủ có chủ ngữ và động từ.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows how much carbon was emitted from gas, oil and coal in the United Kingdom at five points between 1990 and 2010.

Overall, emissions from gas rose steadily and became the highest by 2000, while those from coal declined throughout the period. Oil ended lower than it began, despite a brief rise between 1995 and 2000. Coal was the largest source in 1990, but gas led by the final year.

In 1990, coal produced about 310 million tons of carbon emissions, compared with roughly 270 million tons from oil and 220 million tons from gas. Coal then fell to around 280 million tons in 1995 and 250 million tons in 2000. Gas moved in the opposite direction, rising to about 270 million tons in 1995 and 300 million tons five years later, when it overtook coal. By 2010, gas had climbed further to approximately 320 million tons, slightly above coal’s initial level.

Regarding oil, emissions fell from about 270 million tons in 1990 to 240 million tons in 1995, before recovering to roughly 260 million tons in 2000. They then dropped again to around 240 million tons in 2005 and 210 million tons in 2010. Coal continued to decline over the same final decade, ending at approximately 190 million tons.

review.title: Task 2 · History, science and technology

Bài Task 2 viết tay của NGUYỄN NGỌC CHÂU ANH, trang 2

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Opinions are varied whether History or other subjects such as science and technology are the most essential subjects at school nowadays. Personally, I strongly believed that all academic fields are equally necessary.

Admittedly, history serves as a basis knowledges for students, especially the young children. Initially, the students are exposed to a wide range of knowledge in history, they may be able to know how their countries was founded, the wars the ancient people started in order to protect their nations, the cultures and traditions, which help the youngsters to love and respect the people who defended their country. These students, moreover, become responsible and careful of their actions based on the ancient citizens' mistakes and become a good individual in the future.

On other hand, Science and technology subjects are also a dispensable sectors in students' life. These academic sectors not only equipped students with the valuable knowledge but also develop the nation economy. For example, the founder of Facebook had spent years researching on what people interest in the most in his university, coding a small app for people to socialise and posting status, which resulting in Facebook with huge technological companies across the world nowadays. Furthermore, subjects like Science and technology are both needed in school since they showed students how things work around them, making them more practical, mature and responsible in the real-life world.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that history are as the subjects such as science and technology. Therefore, it would be a unwise decision to overlook one of those subjects.
review.overall: Cô thấy em đã bàn cả lịch sử lẫn khoa học và nói rõ rằng cả hai đều cần ở trường. Em có ví dụ về công nghệ, nhưng cần giải thích nó chứng minh ích lợi của việc học khoa học như thế nào. Trước tiên, hãy sửa chữ “dispensable”, vì từ đó mang nghĩa có thể bỏ đi, trái với lập luận của em. Sau đó tách các câu quá dài và kiểm tra chủ ngữ–động từ.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.comment: Em trả lời cả hai phía và giữ lập trường các môn đều cần; ví dụ Facebook dài nhưng liên hệ với việc dạy môn học chưa đủ rõ.

criteria.label: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.comment: Bốn đoạn có vai trò rõ, song nhiều câu thân bài quá dài, ghép ý và mệnh đề không trọn nên mạch giải thích đứt.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.comment: Có từ vựng theo chủ đề, nhưng “basis knowledges”, “dispensable” và nhiều dạng từ làm nghĩa lệch.

paragraphs.text: Whether schools should give more attention to history or to science and technology remains debated. I believe all three areas are important because they teach students different ways to understand the world and prepare for adulthood.

History provides young people with knowledge of how their communities developed. When students examine the founding of a country or the causes of a past conflict, they learn that decisions have consequences for real people. They can also consider how different groups experienced the same event. This helps them value cultural traditions while thinking carefully about mistakes made in the past. Such lessons may encourage responsibility and empathy, which are useful when students later take part in civic life.

Science and technology are equally necessary. Science teaches students to test explanations against evidence, while technology gives them opportunities to apply that knowledge to practical problems. For example, a pupil who learns coding can design a simple online tool that helps classmates share information. Building it requires logical thinking, testing and revision. These habits matter even if the student does not become a programmer, because digital systems shape work and communication in many fields. Understanding how evidence and digital tools work also helps students judge claims they encounter online instead of simply repeating them. A well-taught science curriculum can therefore support both individual opportunities and the wider economy.

In conclusion, history helps students interpret human experience, whereas science and technology help them investigate and improve their surroundings. Since these benefits complement one another, it would be unwise to remove any of these subjects from school.
